questions.question: Which of the following kitchen substances can be used as an ‘olfactory indicator’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Onion.__

• An **olfactory indicator** is a substance whose **smell varies depending** on whether it is** mixed with an acidic** or **basic solution**.
 
• Olfactory indicators can be used in the **laboratory** to test whether a **solution **is a** base** or an **acid**, a process called **olfactory titration**.
 
• Those substances whose** smell odor** **changes** in **acidic** or **basic** solution are called** olfactory indicators.**
 
• **Onion extract** and **Vanilla extract** are the types of olfactory indicator.
 
• **Two substances are :**
 
 
• **​Onion** has a **great** smell when a basic solution of **sodium hydroxide solution** is added, the** onion smell cannot be detected**. But an **acidic solution** like **HCL** does not **destroy the smell of onion.**
 
• **Vanilla** has a **characteristic smell**. If a basic solution like** sodium hydroxide** is added to** vanilla**, it **can't detect its smell**. But an acidic solution like **HCL** does not **destroy the smell of vanilla extract.**

• It is used in photography. It is also less light-sensitive than halides.

questions.question: Find the work done (in kJ) if a force of 750 N pushes a cart of mass 30 kg by 16 m.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Work is said to be done by a force when the body is displaced actually through some distance in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Since the body is being displaced in the direction of F, therefore work done by the force in displacing the body through a distance s is given by

W = vec F · vec s

Or, W = Fs cos θ

 
• Thus work done by a force is equal to the scalar or dot product of the force and the displacement of the body.

**CALCULATION**__:

Given that:

*⇒ *Force, F = 750 N

*⇒ *displacement, s = 16 m

*⇒ *Work done, w = Fs Cos θ 

Here θ is zero degree so Cos θ = 1

*⇒ W* = 750 × 16

*⇒ W* = 12000 J

To convert Joule into Kilo Joule divide by 1000

*⇒ *w = 12000 / 1000

*⇒ ***Work done, W = 12 KJ**

*⇒ ****__Note:__***** **1 Joule = 0.001 Kilo Joule

questions.question: A certain household has consumed 320 units of energy during a month. How much energy is this in joules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) 1152 x 10⁶ J.

To convert from units of energy (kWh) to joules, we use the formula:

1 kWh = 3.6 x 10⁶ J

So, 320 units of energy is:

320 kWh x 3.6 x 10⁶ J/kWh = 1.152 x 10⁹ J

Therefore, the answer is **1152 x 10⁶ J.**

questions.question: ______ states that for a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component of the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction present in solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raoult’s law**__.

**Raoult’s law** states that a solvent’s partial vapour pressure in a solution (or mixture) is equal or identical to the vapour pressure of the pure solvent multiplied by its mole fraction in the solution.

Mathematically, Raoult’s law equation is written as;

Pₛₒₗᵤₜᵢₒₙ = ΧₛₒₗvₑₙₜP⁰ₛₒₗvₑₙₜ

Where,

Psolution = vapour pressure of the solution

Χₛₒₗvₑₙₜ = mole fraction of the solvent

P⁰ₛₒₗvₑₙₜ = vapour pressure of the pure solvent

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
 

 Boyle’s law
 
 
 
• Boyle’s law, also called Mariotte’s law, a relation concerning the compression and expansion of a gas at a constant temperature.
 
• The pressure exerted by a gas (of a given mass, kept at a constant temperature) is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by it.
 
• The pressure (P) of a given quantity of gas varies inversely with its volume (V) at constant temperature; i.e., in equation form, PV = k, a constant.
 
 
 
 

 Dalton’s law
 
 
 
• The Law of Partial Pressures, states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the gases in the mixture.
 
 
 
 

 Faraday’s law
 
 
 
• Faraday's law of induction (Faraday's law) is a basic law of electromagnetism predicting how a magnetic field will interact with an electric circuit to produce an electromotive force (EMF) - a phenomenon known as electromagnetic induction.
 
• Faraday's law states that the EMF is also given by the rate of change of the magnetic flux:

 [IMAGE: https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/58f8234e421fb6136204fc4785c6a8ffc74d8834] 

 where E is the electromotive force (EMF) and ΦB is the magnetic flux.

questions.question: An incident ray strikes a plane mirror at an angle of 20° with the mirror. The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is ________.
questions.solution:
**__Laws of reflection:__**

1. The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

2. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal lie in the same plane.

3. The reflected ray and the incident ray are on opposite sides of the normal.

__
 
• Angle of reflection = ∠r
 
• Angle of incidence = ∠i
 
• The angle between the plane mirror and incident ray = 20°

According Law of reflection:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba310ec8a33b6876833335a27b7097d2a4c6dd55c6f634934519a02c7c8ffb23.png] 

 
• 20° + ∠r + ∠i + 20° = 180°
 
• ∠r + ∠i = 140°
 
• The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is **140°.__**

questions.question: The ability of a cell to divide into two equal daughter cells is called_________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****__binary fission__**.

__
 
• The ability of a cell to divide into two equal daughter cells is called **binary fission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The organism duplicates the genetic material, or deoxyribonucleic acid ( DNA), in the binary fission process and then breaks into two parts (cytokinesis), each new organism receiving a single copy of DNA.
 
• **Multicellular fragmentation** is a type of asexual reproduction in which an organism is divided into fragments.
 
• **Multiple fission **is the asexual reproduction process, in which many daughter cells are produced from the parent cell instead of 2 daughter cells.
 
• **Budding **is a form of asexual reproduction in which, due to cell division at one particular location, a new organism emerges from an outgrowth or bud.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Fragmentation, multiple fission, binary fission, and budding are all types of asexual reproduction methods in organisms.

 
• **Fragmentation:** This is a form of asexual reproduction where a new organism grows from a fragment of the parent. Each fragment develops into a mature, fully grown individual. This occurs in many organisms such as starfish, sea anemones, and planaria, as well as in many plants, fungi and bacteria.
 
• **Multiple Fission**: In this method, an organism divides into many new individuals simultaneously. The parent organism undergoes cytokinesis (cell division) to form several daughter cells. This is common in some protists like Plasmodium (the organism that causes malaria) and certain types of algae.
 
• **Binary Fission:** In this mode of reproduction, a parent organism, usually a single cell, splits into two separate cells. Binary fission takes place in many unicellular organisms such as bacteria and protozoa.
 
• **Budding**: This is a form of asexual reproduction in which a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud on another one. The new organism remains attached to the parent organism to begin with, eventually separating and living independently. Budding is common in yeast and hydra.

questions.question: The magnetic field outside a very tightly wound long solenoid is considered to be ___________.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Solenoid: A solenoid is a conducting wire wound into coils of many turns forming a cylindrical shape such that its diameter is less compared to its length.

 
 
• Each turn of the coil is treated as a closed circular loop, hence the magnetic field produced from it is considered as that produced by a circular current-carrying conductor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66c63a320693aee608bfb76cdaeae8cbdefbe60ab7c33084913e066e5e5ff237.png] 

B={{{mu }₀}NI}

Where N = number of turns per unit length, l = current in the solenoid, and μo = absolute permeability of air or vacuum.

The field lines due to current in a circular loop are as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4515f230cbbfe4d0bad8a577b4f4a5ee29383990959fb93e3409826e2c2fd23f.png] 

 
• The net magnetic field in a solenoid is, therefore, equal to the vector sum of the magnetic field due to each loop.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• The magnetic field line is a straight line inside a solenoid. Hence, it remains uniform along its length.
 
• The magnetic field inside a solenoid is the sum of magnetic fields due to all loops. So, on increasing the number of loops, the number of electrons causing current increases. Thus magnetic field strength increases.
 
• The distance from the current-carrying conductor and the magnetic field are inversely proportional. Thus, towards the ends of the solenoid, the magnetic field strength reduces as they diverge.
 
• The magnetic field outside the solenoid is zero.

questions.question: In human body, the food passes through a continuous canal which begins at ______ and ends at anus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**buccal cavity.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The human digestive system consists of a continuous **canal** through which food passes.
 
• The **canal begins at the buccal cavity and ends at the anus.**
 
• **Human Digestion system-**
 
 
• ​The human digestive system consists of several organs and structures involved in the process of digestion.
 
• The **canal begins at the buccal cavity,** also known as the **mouth or oral cavity**, where **food enters the body.**
 
• After being chewed and mixed with **saliva**, the food is formed into a small, soft mass called a **bolus**.
 
• The bolus then passes through the pharynx, which is the junction between the buccal cavity and the esophagus.
 
• From the pharynx, the food travels down the **esophagus**, also known as the **food pipe or the gullet.**
 
• The esophagus is a muscular tube that propels food toward the stomach through rhythmic contractions called peristalsis.
 
• Once the food reaches the stomach, it undergoes further digestion through the action of **stomach acids and enzymes.**
 
• The stomach mixes the food with **gastric juices** and breaks it down into a **semi-liquid mixture called chyme.**
 
• The chyme is then gradually released into the **small intestine, the longest part of the digestive tract.**
 
• In the small intestine, the majority of nutrient **absorption **takes place, aided by specialized structures called **villi**.
 
• The small intestine consists of three sections: the **duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.**
 
• After passing through the small intestine, the remaining waste material enters the large intestine, also known as the **colon**.
 
• In the large intestine, water and electrolytes are absorbed from the waste, forming solid feces.
 
• The feces are stored in the rectum until they are eliminated from the body through the **anus** during the process of **defecation**.

questions.question: According to which of the following laws, the pressure of a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the component gases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dalton's Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dalton's Law:**

 
 
• **Definition: **Dalton's Law, also known as the Law of Partial Pressures, states that **the total pressure exerted by a mixture of gases is the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases.**
 
• **Partial Pressure: **The pressure that each gas would exert if it alone occupied the entire volume of the mixture is its partial pressure.
 
• **Independent Behaviour: **The law assumes that gases behave independently of each other, meaning the pressure of each gas in a mixture is unaffected by the presence of other gases.
 
• **Applications: **Dalton's Law has important applications in many areas including chemistry, physics, physiology, and even scuba diving, where understanding the pressures of different gas components is crucial.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Law
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Charles' Law
 States that the volume of a given mass of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature provided its pressure remains constant.
 
 

 Boyle's Law
 Proposes an inverse relationship between the pressure and volume of a gas, assuming the temperature is kept constant within a closed system.
 
 

 Graham's Law
 
 
Describes the relationship between the rates of diffusion of gases and their molar masses.

 
It states that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.

questions.question: Which of the following chemicals is released by ants onto the skin of a human-being when they bite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CH2O2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ants release **formic acid** (CH2O2) onto the skin when they bite.
 
• Formic acid is also known as **methanoic acid**.
 
• It is the simplest **carboxylic acid** with the chemical formula HCOOH.
 
• Formic acid appears as a **colorless liquid** with a pungent odor.
 
• The term "formic" originates from the Latin word **'formica'**, meaning ant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formic Acid in Nature**

 
 
• Formic acid is present in **most ants** and stingless bees.
 
• It is used by ants as a **defense mechanism** against predators.
 
 
 
• **Other Acids and Their Sources**
 
 
• **Lactic Acid** – Found in curd and sour milk products.
 
• **Oxalic Acid** – Present in tea, spinach, and tomatoes.
 
• **Tartaric Acid** – Found in grapes, tamarind, and gooseberries.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Formic Acid**
 
 
• Used in **textile and leather processing**.
 
• Employed as a **preservative** and antibacterial agent in livestock feed.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions**
 
 
• Formic acid can cause **skin irritation** and should be handled with care.
 
• In case of contact, **wash the area with water** immediately.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a type of connective tissue?

I. Blood

II. Bone

III. Ligament
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Connective tissues** provide** structural support and integrity **to the body, with diverse types such as** loose, dense, adipose, cartilage, bone, and blood,** each contributing unique properties and functions within the extracellular matrix. ***Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.***
 
• The **extracellular matrix,** composed of protein fibres and ground substance, determines the **flexibility, strength, and elasticity of connective tissues,** allowing them to adapt to different mechanical demands.
 
• Apart from their structural roles, connective tissues also play a **crucial role in immunity,** with certain types housing immune cells and contribute to immune responses** against pathogens and foreign substances.**
 
• Connective tissues are essential components of the body, contributing to its **overall architecture, supporting organs and tissues, storing energy, protecting vital structures,** and participating in various **physiological processes.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood:**

 
 
• Blood is a type of **connective tissue **that consists of cells suspended in a** liquid matrix called plasma.**
 
• It plays a vital role in** transporting oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products** throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Bone: **
 
 
• Bone is a specialized** connective tissue** that forms the **skeletal structure of the body.**
 
• It provides **support, protection, and facilitates movement. **
 
• Bone tissue is composed of cells called** osteocytes** embedded in a matrix of **collagen fibres and calcium salts.**
 
 
 
• **Ligament: **
 
 
• Ligaments are **fibrous connective tissues** that connect bones to other bones in a joint.
 
• They provide **stability** and help** limit excessive movement **within the joint, contributing to joint strength and function.
